outcome: Prevalence of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS)
cohort: Pregnant women over the age of 18 years booked for shared antenatal care at a district general hospital in the UK.
finding: The antenatal period may represent an important opportunity for health promotion and intervention as there is a high prevalence of LUTS in the antenatal population.
mod_finding: Women were almost four times more likely to report any type of urinary incontinence if they had had a vaginal birth in their first pregnancy compared to those who had a caesarean section and women who had a forceps delivery were seven times more likely to report incontinence.
